summary.text: Paul Pate is Iowa's Republican Secretary of State and is seeking re-election in 2026. A small business owner by background, he has held the office from 1995 to 1999 and again since 2015. He says he is running on a layered approach to election security, including voter ID, paper ballots and post-election audits, alongside business-filing modernization.

paragraphs.text: Pate was born in Ottumwa, Iowa, and earned an associate degree from Kirkwood Community College in 1978.
He works as a small business owner and describes himself as the third-generation owner of his family's asphalt business.
Pate first served as Iowa Secretary of State from 1995 to 1999, and he took the office again on January 1, 2015.
In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he says he also served as a state senator and as a mayor.
He says he earned a CERA election-administration designation while in office.
Pate cites among his accomplishments a Fast Track Filing system that he says cut business filing times from weeks to minutes, a redesigned website and a 24-hour call center.
He also says he worked with the legislature to create Safe at Home, an address confidentiality program for survivors of violent crime.
Pate won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary and faces Democrat Ryan Peterman in the November 3 general election.
